text:
Alex (support): Heads up — multiple staging deploys started failing after we rolled the CI service account token this morning. Error shows up when the pipeline hits Redwood API to upload model artifacts: 401 Unauthorized.

Alex (support): Full snippet from the CI job (redacted):
```
Uploading artifact to https://api.redwood.example/v1/models/upload
Authorization: Bearer $CI_DEPLOY_TOKEN
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "message": "token has insufficient scopes: missing models:write"
}
```

Alex (support): This looks like a scope/permission problem (token rotation replaced a long-lived key that used to have broader scopes). The customer noticed their merge -> deploy pipeline started failing right after we rotated the token. They rotated because the former token was expired/compromised.

Priya (platform eng): Thanks Alex. Do we know which service-account was used? Is this the `ci-deploy-bot` service account or the old `deploy-service` user?

Alex (support): It's the internal `ci-deploy-bot` (used by our GitLab runner). The token was created via `rwctl tokens create` and then stored in the project's secrets. The token metadata (from our audit logs) shows TTL=168h and scopes were set to `deploy:*` only — missing `models:write` apparently.

Diego (sre): Quick triage: if the API says missing `models:write` then we should either: 1) mint a replacement token with expanded scopes (quick fix), or 2) modify the CI job to call the artifact upload via an infra proxy that has proper perms (longer). For now surface the least-privilege fix we can do safely.

Priya (platform eng): Agreed. Can you try re-creating a token with explicit scopes and very short TTL (1h) and test in a single job run? Example command (internal CLI):
```
# create 1-hour token with minimal required scopes for artifact upload
rwctl tokens create --service-account=ci-deploy-bot --scopes=models:write,deploy:trigger --ttl=1h
```
Replace the secret in the project's CI variables and re-run the job. If that passes, we can then determine a longer-term policy.

Alex (support): Doing that now. Will update when I have results. Also adding repro steps for customer: 1) Merge to branch -> pipeline runs -> job fails at upload step with 401; 2) Job log shows `missing models:write`; 3) Workaround: push a manually-created token with proper scope.

ci-bot: Job #2024 re-run started by Alex (support) at staging.gitlab.example

Alex (support): Re-run failed with same 401 even after replacing secret — investigating. Here's the exact token-introspection output we got from rwctl: 
```
rwctl tokens introspect --token=xxxxx
{
  "active": true,
  "scopes": ["deploy:trigger"],
  "service_account": "ci-deploy-bot",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-15T12:40:00Z"
}
```

Alex (support): Introspection claims active but scopes don't include `models:write` even though I supplied it in the create command. Huh. Maybe we have a policy that strips certain scopes for internal SSO-linked accounts?

Priya (platform eng): That's suspicious. Two possibilities: 1) the token creation command is being invoked under an identity that has constrained scope grants (e.g., caller lacks permission to grant models:write), or 2) there's an enforcement policy on the service account that pins its allowed scopes. Check the admin audit/event log around token creation — it usually contains fields `requested_scopes` and `granted_scopes`.

Diego (sre): Also check the governance rules: `service-accounts.yml` for `ci-deploy-bot` may include `allowed_scopes: [deploy:trigger]` which would strip extra scopes at mint time. If that's the case, we need an admin override or update the policy.

Alex (support): I pulled the audit entry: `requested_scopes=[models:write,deploy:trigger]` but `granted_scopes=[deploy:trigger]`. The entry also has `created_by=ci-admin` and `policy_action=scope_rewrite`.

Priya (platform eng): OK that confirms a policy rewrite. Why is that policy in place? Historically we locked model write to human-approved flows because model uploads touch customer data and are more sensitive. We need a process to allow CI bot to do uploads safely. Options: - add an environment-scoped exception for staging, - create a separate `artifact-uploader` service account with explicit allowed_scopes including models:write but limited to staging project, or - require the CI job to push artifacts to an internal artifact proxy that then uploads using a curated account.

Alex (support): Customer expects a short-term fix for staging. Which option is fastest?

Priya (platform eng): Fastest: create a new short-lived service account token for `artifact-uploader` with allowed_scopes `[models:write]` and a tight resource restriction (project=staging-only). We can script token creation and add to CI secrets for that repo only. I'll create the PR to the `service-accounts.yml` allowlist, but we can do a temporary admin override now.

Diego (sre): One more thing — audit/rotation: ensure the token TTL <= 2h for temporary usage, and add automated rotation in the pipeline so we don't leave long-lived secrets. Also recommend switching the GitLab runner to OIDC if possible to avoid storing long-lived tokens.

Alex (support): Admin override worked — I minted an `artifact-uploader` token with models:write and TTL 2h and put it in staging secrets. Re-ran pipeline: upload step now succeeds. Customer confirmed staging deploy green. :tada:

Priya (platform eng): Great. Next steps:
- Priya: open PR to update service-accounts policy to allow `artifact-uploader` for staging with explicit allowed_scopes and resource limits. (will include justification + risk assessment)
- Diego: document a runbook for CI token creation, introspection, and troubleshooting (include `rwctl tokens introspect` examples, how to read audit logs, sample minimal scopes).
- Alex: follow up with customer on recommended long-term approach (OIDC or artifact proxy).

Alex (support): Will send customer note with workaround and timeline. Also logging a support ticket to track follow-up.

infra-bot: PR #452 created by Priya to service-accounts allowlist (WIP).

Priya (platform eng): One policy note: we should not relax global `models:write` grant for CI bots. Create narrow-scoped service accounts per environment/project. I'll add examples and a template for `service-accounts.yml`.

Diego (sre): Also adding a CI lint step that checks for use of `REDACTED_TOKEN` or other long-lived creds in repo variables and warns if TTL > 24h. That should catch accidental long-lived tokens.

Alex (support): Thanks team. I'll close the incident once the PR is merged and the runbook is live. If anyone needs me to coordinate with the customer's SRE, ping me. :thumbsup:
